text:
marta (support): Heads up — we started seeing a spike of 502/504s for hosted-api via the edge at ~10:05 PDT. 502s ~12x baseline, 504s ~6x. Affects streaming and chunked responses.

jason (eng-sre): Any correlated deploys or key rotations around that time? can you paste a sample trace id and a curl repro?

marta (support): No deploys on the timeline. We did have an auth token rotation scheduled at 10:00 that finished ~10:03. Sample trace id: trace=01e4f2a3. Repro curl (sanitized):

```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <short-lived>" \
  -H "X-Request-Id: trace-01e4f2a3" \
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate" \
  -d '{"model":"open-xxl","input":"test"}'
```

Result: upstream reset, status 502, body empty.

ken (ingress): Looking at Envoy stats now — upstream connection saturation metrics spiked right after the rotation. h2 conn counts + long-lived streams. Possible keepalive pool exhaustion + client retries amplifying.

deploy-bot: ALERT: ingress-frontend autoscale triggered (scale from 6 -> 12) at 10:08 due to CPU > 80%

carla (customer-success): Affected tenant reported timeouts for batch embeddings and long-poll streaming. They were sending larger chunk sizes during their nightly job.

jason (eng-sre): Two-pronged hypothesis: 1) auth rotation caused a subset of requests to get rejected at auth proxy, clients retried quickly short-circuiting to the edge; 2) many simultaneous long lived streams exhausted keepalive conn pool -> Envoy returning 502/504 to new requests.

marta (support): Can we get the exact Envoy stat names and quick mitigation steps? Customers are escalating.

ken (ingress): Check these metrics: upstream_cx_total, upstream_cx_active, upstream_rq_pending_overflow, http2.rx_total_streams, and pool queue sizes. Quick fixes:
- Temporarily increase envoy upstream connection pool size for ingress host pool
- Lower per-client concurrency (rate cap) for tenants doing big batches
- Enable retry budget to avoid retry storms
- Rollback auth rotation or enable fallback tokens if available

jason (eng-sre): Commands (cluster admin):
```
# kubectl patch to bump pool size (example)
kubectl -n edge patch deploy/ingress-frontend --type='json' -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/env/0/value","value":"POOL_SIZE=120"}]'
```

ken (ingress): Also added a temporary Envoy config tweak on canary: increase per-host connection limit to 200 and lower idle stream timeout to 30s. Pushed to 2/6 pods as canary at 10:20. Monitoring.

marta (support): After the canary push 10:25-10:35 we saw 502s drop ~70% for affected tenants. Still some tail 504s from long streams.

carla (customer-success): I told the tenant to pause that nightly job and to chunk their embeddings smaller as an interim step. They confirmed fewer errors on their side.

jason (eng-sre): Longer term actions to prevent recurrence:
- Harden auth rotation: staggered rollout + sticky token TTL to avoid mass invalidations
- Add admission control to limit bursty long-lived streams per tenant
- Improve observability: surface per-tenant upstream queue and conn metrics in console

marta (support): Documenting repro steps and mitigation in the ticket. Will follow up with postmortem if we keep the metrics.

ken (ingress): Leaving the canary config for 30m, if stable we'll promote. If we still see retries causing saturation, we should add retry_throttle and circuit-breaker for long-stream endpoints.

marta (support): Thanks — closing the urgent incident channel for now, will reopen if 502/504 rate rises. :white_check_mark:
